title: deriveFactId's hash material uses an unescaped "|" delimiter (`${studentId}|${key}|${canonicalJson(value)}|${sessionId ?? ""}`); studentId and key are both unrestricted z.string().min(1) (packages/schemas), so a "|" inside either field lets two DIFFERENT (studentId,key) pairs derive the identical fact _id
evidence: direct read-only execution of the worktree's own packages/db/src/facts.ts via tsx (no edit made): deriveFactId("alice|X","c","v","s") === deriveFactId("alice","X|c","v","s") -> true (identical sha256). Consequence traced through applyApprovedDiff: activeFilter still matches on the real studentId/key fields (no false idempotent match), but the colliding _id would hit Mongo's built-in unique _id index on insertOne (E11000), and the subsequent re-read against activeFilter for the true (studentId,key) finds no matching doc, so the code falls to the else branch and throws FactConflictError for a legitimate, non-conflicting write -- a correctness gap, not a crash, and it requires a literal "|" character inside studentId or key, which nothing currently prevents.
fix: use a collision-safe encoding for the hash material -- e.g. hash each field separately and concatenate the hashes, JSON.stringify the tuple, or escape/length-prefix each segment before joining -- plus a regression test with a "|" embedded in studentId or key

title: resumeScribe forking from an already-resolved pre-approval checkpoint silently discards a second, DIFFERENT resume decision and replays the cached (original) decision instead, reporting success with the stale value
evidence: qa/verdicts/t-007-scribe-graph.md cycle 0 -- checker's own probe (scratchpad t007-probes/p3-fork-diagnostic.ts, run with tsx against the unmodified worktree, MockProvider + MemorySaver + fakes.ts, offline): after startScribe + resumeScribe({action:'approve'}) writes fact F (Canada), the checker fetched the pre-approval checkpoint id via getStateHistory and called graph.invoke(new Command({resume:{action:'reject', reason:'checker fork probe'}}), {configurable:{thread_id, checkpoint_id: pausedCheckpointId}}) directly. The raw invoke() return value shows decision:{approve:true, edits:[...the ORIGINAL Canada fact...]} and result.status:'written' with the SAME writtenFactIds as the first approval -- the 'reject' action was silently ignored. getStateHistory shows two sibling checkpoints forked from the same parent (the paused interrupt), both independently reaching the identical decision/result, proving the second branch's own counsellor_approval node execution did not honour the new Command.resume value. No B3 violation (no unapproved value is written -- the written value was genuinely approved once), but the reported outcome does not match the submitted decision, which is misleading (B14 concern) and untested by the maker's own D-012 fork test (which only ever resubmits an IDENTICAL decision, so it cannot distinguish real DB-layer idempotent replay via contentHash from LangGraph checkpoint-level caching of an already-resolved interrupt task).
fix: before T-008 (counsellor UI) or any retry/admin tool is built on ScribeRunOptions.checkpointId, add a test for the divergent-decision-at-same-checkpoint case and either (a) guard against it explicitly (throw instead of silently discarding the new resume value), or (b) document plainly in checkpointId's docstring that a checkpoint's interrupt resolution is one-shot / cached, and a second different resume value at the same checkpoint is not honoured -- callers needing a genuine 'redo the approval' must not reuse the same checkpoint id.

Independently re-verified with my own probe (scratchpad t007c2-checker-probes.ts, probe 5, distinct scenarios from the maker's and prior checker's tests): scalar 'a' matches every doc whose tags array contains it plus a scalar-equal doc, a non-existent scalar matches nothing, an array filter ['a','b'] matches only the exactly-ordered array (a reversed ['b','a'] array does NOT match it), and an empty array field never falsely matches. Also confirmed via my own falsification (scratchpad t007c2-checker-falsify.py, F4): forcing the array-contains branch to 'return false' turns the maker's ISS-t-007-c1-1 db test RED (fail=1), and restoring it returns the full db suite (9/9 relevant, 73/73 overall) to green. Stable across 5 repeated full runs. The prior finding (both callers told done/written) no longer reproduces.

(checker, t-007 cycle 2) graph.ts:resumeScribe closes the TOCTOU (senior Block, reproduced in cycle 1) with an atomic claim: an insertOne into scribe_resolutions (_id=threadId, unique index on threadId, no partial filter -- packages/db/scripts/db-init.ts INDEX_PLAN, confirmed by reading the plan directly) runs before graph.invoke; on 11000 the loser re-reads the winning claim and returns already_resolved with the WINNER's decision (never its own) and a sameAsWinner flag; the loser never invokes the graph, so there is one claim, one invoke, no double write. Crash-after-claim recovery: resumeScribe(null) resumes with the CLAIMED response when a claim exists and the interrupt is still pending, is idempotent on a second call, and a rival response in between gets already_resolved with result:null (winner still in flight) and the CLAIMED decision.
